$comment: UMB-048. private-working repos are PRIVATE — several GitHub security features are N/A there, not skipped by oversight; the org is on GitHub Team since 2026-11-16, which adds rulesets on private repos (the organization ruleset below) but not secret scanning or code scanning (paid add-ons, not bought). Encoded from the same source, main's 2026-09-03 REST apply against template-private-working (which hit exactly these N/A cases live: a 403 on the ruleset endpoint).

allowAutoMerge.reason: UMB-062: PATCH {"allow_auto_merge":true} on a free-org PRIVATE repo returns HTTP 200 but the field reads back false on a subsequent GET — measured live on Chotmeter and Bankfire, 2026-09-04 18:55, and re-confirmed by a read-only GET the same day (both still show allow_auto_merge:false). GitHub's own REST reference and product docs do not document a plan- or visibility-tier restriction for this field (checked, not found) — encoded as MEASURED, not as an explained mechanism. Do not retry the PATCH expecting a different result on this org's current plan; if the org's plan or this repo's visibility ever changes, re-measure before trusting either this N/A or a restored true.

secretScanning.reason: Secret scanning on a PRIVATE repo needs GitHub Secret Protection, a paid add-on this org does not carry (GitHub Team does not include it). Measured live on template-private-working, 2026-09-03 — do not retry the enable call; it will 403/422 every time on this plan tier.

privateVulnerabilityReporting.reason: GitHub restricts private vulnerability reporting to PUBLIC repos only. A private-working repo cannot enable this regardless of plan.

ruleset.reason: Not written per repo: every private repo is covered by the ORGANIZATION ruleset private-main-guard (id 27358894; deletion + non_fast_forward on the default branch; targets visibility = private; empty bypass list, the recovery being the owner disabling it for one operation), created 2026-11-16 on GitHub Team. A new private repo is covered the day it exists, so this apply writes nothing for it. On the Free plan a private repo has no ruleset (POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets answered 403 on template-private-working, 2026-09-03). SERIES-CANON.md, Repository rulesets.
ruleset.$ifItEverBecomesAvailableNote: the caveat from repo-settings.published-code.json's ruleset.$noRequiredStatusChecksNote applies identically the day this becomes applicable — gate.yml's own steps are hashFiles-gated the same way ci.yml's are (the .github commit da15148 red-fix covers all three kinds), so a future required-status-check here should name the 'gate' job, never a step inside it.

tagRuleset.reason: Not set: the organization ruleset private-main-guard covers the default branch only. A tag ruleset on a private repo is available on GitHub Team and is not part of the private canon (SERIES-CANON.md, Repository rulesets); on the Free plan it answered 403 (measured 2026-09-24 on every private repo in the org).
